title.narrative: Self-sufficiency of Sudanese refugees in three camps in eastern Chad and support to the local pop.

description.narrative: Since the start of the Darfur conflict in 2003, about 260,000 Sudanese refugees have been living in 12 camps in the east of Chad under the mandate of the UNHCR. SECADEV is a relief and development organisation set up by the Diocese of Njamena in 1983 and has been operational in eastern Chad since 1986. SECADEV manages three camps as a UNHCR partner (Kounoungou, Farchana and Milé) and is supported financially by the Caritas Confederation and by OFDA. The project aims to develop self-sufficiency of refugees from Darfur in the three camps in eastern Chad managed by SECADEV and to provide water to the local population in 12 local villages. There are five specific sectors of activity: (i) water: refugees and the local population have access to drinking water and water from shallow wells in the villages and take part in the management of water distribution. (ii) sanitation: the camp environment is improved through the greater participation of the refugees. (iii) education: school attendance and conditions for learning are improved. (iv) community mobilisation: refugees develop social and cultural activities which will promote better co-existence. (v) domestic and household support: refugees and people with specific needs in the camps receive household items and accessories which enable them to live in dignity. CRS is CI's lead agency in Chad but Secours Catholique has played a crucial role in the accompaniment and capacity-building of SECADEV which has enabled the organsiation to manage a large relief programme. The project corresponds to Caritas EA10/2009 with a total budget of €1,923 077. This appeal has already been supported by Caritas Denmark, Switzerland, and Secours Catholique. CAFOD has supported previous appeals for this target group implemented by SECADEV in 2007 and 2008 when the accompaniment from Secours Catholique added to the capacity of the partner.
